summary: Incremental usage indexing gap causes spurious rate alerts on console
description:
Issue summary: Customer (Fjord Health) reports repeated rate alerts fired from the Console for a weekly throughput SLO despite backend ingestion showing normal request counts. Impact: Customer-facing alerts triggered automated paging and blocked key dashboards; billing reconciliation checks also flagged potential overages. Environment: Production, us-east-1 cluster, org-scoped rollups for last14d.

Observed behaviour: Starting 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC, console alerts that evaluate based on per-minute rate metrics (derived from the incremental usage index) started firing in 15–30 minute waves covering multiple orgs including Fjord Health. The raw API request logs and serving runtime metrics show steady traffic; the raw events count in Kafka and the downstream aggregation jobs do not show spikes. The console metric graphs show sudden drops in the underlying rate series, followed by sharp re-populations when a backfill job completes (~10–20 minutes later).

Expected behaviour: Incremental indexing should provide near-real-time upserts to the usage index without gaps; alerts based on rate thresholds should only fire when actual request rate breaches the configured SLO. Backfills should not cause transient missing data that make console evaluators treat recent windows as zero.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided + reproduced internally): 1) Org with steady traffic over 24h and an active per-minute rate alert configured (threshold at 25% drop). 2) Reload console timeframe to last 15 minutes and observe alert state toggling. 3) Query ingestion consumer lag and index commit timestamps during an observed window; reproduce by temporarily pausing the incremental index updater in staging and restarting it to simulate delayed commits.

Logs & artifacts: - Console alert history: attached screenshot (customer) and evaluator trace id a1b2c3d4. - Ingestion consumer offsets show periodic gap between commit time and event timestamp (~9–12 minutes) for the incremental index writer. - Backfill job run logs show successful replays completing and writing missing buckets. - Linked alerts: SUP-41234 (alert-eval-window-drift) noted similar symptom but tied to DST in that case.

Initial hypothesis: A race condition in the incremental indexer (ingestion/commit/flush path) can leave short-lived time buckets empty when high-volume writes and compaction coincide with the index writer's commit cadence. Console evaluators treat missing buckets as zeros for rate-based alerts. Backfill/repair runs repopulate the buckets, causing the console metric to recover and alert to auto-resolve.

Impact assessment: Multiple enterprise customers were paged during a 3-hour window; internal pager fatigue and customer trust degradation. Billing reconciliation scripts flagged the orgs briefly for apparent sudden drops in usage. No evidence of dropped requests at serving runtime layer.

Temporary workaround: We advised the customer to widen the alert evaluation window and switch alerts to use the 5m rolling average until fix is deployed. Support also suggested excluding the incremental index as a primary source for critical paging until repair is validated.

Next actions (triage): 1) Assign ingestion/analytics on-call to capture a live reproduction (Liam). 2) Add additional logging around indexer commit latency and bucket tombstone markers. 3) Create controlled staging test where incremental writer pause is simulated. 4) Implement change to console evaluator to treat missing buckets as "unknown" rather than 0 for evaluation if index freshness < X. 5) Run a reconciliation sweep to repair recently impacted orgs.

Requested owner: analytics-pipeline team.

Notes: Customer asked for a post-incident note describing which alerts fired and the time slices affected for their internal SRE postmortem.
